findings.title: Current packaging omits tag queries and relies on checkout-dependent asset lookup

evidence.detail: Tag queries are bare filenames, no longer bundled .scm imports.
Queries load through filesystem candidates including the module and executable directory.
Dynamic dirname falls back to require.resolve(@codebuff/code-map), which current Bun bundles resolve to the build checkout.
The .scm loader remains, but no .scm file is imported by the language table.
SDK packaging copies WASM and vendor files; it never copies the query directory.
Required grammar assets are copied to dist/wasm.
Binary builder explicitly creates sibling tree-sitter-queries directory.
Matrix tar member list includes binary, WASMs and manifest, but excludes query directory.
Windows tar member list excludes query directory too.
Token scoring requires both parser and query; missing query becomes parse_error.

findings.trigger: Publish current SDK dist or install current CLI release archive on a machine without the build checkout or incidental query directory.
findings.consequence: Grammar existence does not establish semantic availability: installed query-driven symbol/call/import captures disappear; SDK default grammar resolution can also miss copied assets. AST structural outlines can still work when a grammar loads.
findings.suggestedFix: Anchor assets to the actual package/executable location; copy and checksum query files in SDK, both release archives and wrapper-managed siblings; retain caller-supplied setWasmDir behavior.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Build current SDK ESM/CJS, npm-pack and extract it and both platform archives into isolated fixtures; remove build-source visibility; assert parser/query and nonempty symbols/calls for every advertised grammar without network or cwd-dependent files.
findings.observedEvidence: Source builder/archive mismatch plus fresh current-source component bundles in evidence/07-assets.json. Default PHP parser false in both Node formats; explicit pinned WASM directory enables it while retained checkout supplies queries.
findings.inferenceLimits: Component bundle probe is not a full SDK release build. CLI installed-wrapper context at cli/release/index.js:52-68 omits query directories, but that file is deliberately excluded from structuralReceipt. No release bug is inferred merely from failing development asset tests.
findings.markdownParagraph: HIGH — The binary builder creates `tree-sitter-queries/` (`cli/scripts/build-binary.ts:658`), but both release tar lists omit it (`.github/workflows/cli-release-build.yml:460,644`). SDK packaging copies WASM without queries (`sdk/scripts/build.ts:147,508`); its old `.scm` loader cannot embed bare filenames. Runtime lookup also depends on dynamically resolving the internal code-map package (`packages/code-map/src/utils.ts:25`). Missing queries remove scoring and call/import captures, although AST outlines may survive. Isolated package/archive probes must require actual semantic output, preserve explicit directory overrides, and avoid build-checkout visibility.

findings.trigger: Use Python/Rust/Go/etc. bare extensions in the shared helper or index a Python call and a Rust same-name definition.

findings.title: Post-edit LSP synchronization can reuse versions and leave opened documents stale

evidence.detail: On-demand query opens a document at connection-local version1.
Separate service version LRU does not observe that open; eviction resets next counter.

findings.trigger: Query a file before its first edit, overflow the64-entry service version LRU, or edit an already-open path beyond the32-path/1MiB sync bounds.
findings.consequence: didChange can reuse/decrease a version; a conforming server may discard it. Skipped already-open files remain stale because later queries only reopen unopened URIs.
findings.suggestedFix: Make version authority connection-local and shared by query/sync; close/invalidate dirty skipped paths and reopen from committed bytes on demand; report per-path sync outcomes and bounds.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Strict fake peer plus real-server query->edit->query must see committed bytes and strictly increasing versions; exercise65+ paths,33-file edit batches, oversized changed documents, failures and restart.

findings.inferenceLimits: The strict fake confirms protocol violation and reachable stale observation; individual real servers may tolerate duplicate versions. WorkspaceEdit mutation normalization remains pair06 scope.
findings.markdownParagraph: HIGH — Query opening uses connection version 1 (`lsp-multiplexer.ts:1040`), while post-edit sync starts a separate counter at 1 (`language-intelligence.ts:979`). The strict peer rejected that first `didChange` and returned old hover text after disk changed. LRU eviction also resets counters without reopening (`:593`), and capped or oversized already-open files remain stale. The existing version test observes a fake multiplexer, missing this integration. Share document/version authority and invalidate skipped dirty documents so later queries reread committed bytes.

findings.title: Malformed transport teardown and delayed restart can orphan language-server processes

evidence.detail: Frame overflow calls handleGone; malformed headers do likewise at495.
handleGone clears child without terminating it.
killChild cannot kill a child after the handle was cleared.
Restart sleeps, starts a fresh connection, then assigns it without disposed/entry ownership checks.
Dispose stops currently registered connections and clears map without joining restart promises.
Production run cleanup uses mux disposal.

findings.trigger: A still-live peer emits malformed/oversized framing; dispose occurs during its200ms restart delay.
findings.consequence: Original process loses its kill handle; replacement can start after disposal and never be registered/reaped. Reported pool bounds and run cleanup no longer bound actual processes.
findings.suggestedFix: Separate observed exit from transport failure; retain/terminate/reap child before clearing it. Cancel/join restarts and check disposed plus entry ownership before spawning/publishing.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Under malformed framing and dispose during backoff/startup, every spawned fake child receives termination; a real bounded child fixture leaves no surviving PID or pending timer and no post-dispose spawn.
findings.observedEvidence: Evidence/07-probes.json reports spawnCount2, killCounts[0,0], warmServerCount0 after malformed header then dispose.
findings.inferenceLimits: Fake handles measure missed termination calls. No hostile process or OS sandbox exploit was tested.
findings.markdownParagraph: HIGH — Framing failures call `handleGone`, which clears the child without killing it (`sdk/src/services/lsp-multiplexer.ts:572`). The delayed restart does not check disposal before starting its replacement (`:961`); disposal joins neither restart nor replacement (`:1443`). The probe produced two fake children, zero kill calls, and a reported pool size of zero. Preserve handles through termination, cancel and join restarts, and require ownership checks before publication. Pool counts alone cannot serve as process-lifetime evidence.

findings.title: A first root marker in the file parent can be overwritten by an ancestor marker

evidence.detail: Marker search starts from parent for each marker.

findings.trigger: pkg/tsconfig.json sits next to pkg/doc.ts while root/package.json is an ancestor later-listed marker.
findings.consequence: Wrong cwd/rootUri and pool key select the ancestor server instead of the documented first-marker root.
findings.suggestedFix: Track found explicitly or return immediately on a successful marker, including the file-parent directory; document marker priority versus nearest-directory policy.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Parent first marker must win over ancestor later marker; preserve existing priority, subtree sharing, TTL invalidation and nested root fixtures.
findings.observedEvidence: Evidence/07-probes.json expected roots/pkg but defaultRootResolver returned roots.
findings.inferenceLimits: This finding challenges a branch error, not the intentional first-marker priority policy.
findings.markdownParagraph: MEDIUM — `defaultRootResolver` stops only when its selected root differs from the starting parent (`sdk/src/services/lsp-multiplexer.ts:668`). A matching `pkg/tsconfig.json` beside the queried file leaves that comparison false; the later ancestor `package.json` overwrites it. The fixture reproduced the wrong root. Track successful discovery explicitly and cover parent-directory matches, preserving the documented priority policy and cache behavior.

findings.title: Grouped profile IDs are sent as LSP document language identifiers

evidence.detail: TypeScript profile groups JS/JSX/TSX.
C/C++ profile groups C source.
Server routing uses grouped registry ID.
On-demand didOpen forwards grouped ID directly.
Sync didOpen does likewise.

findings.trigger: Open .js/.jsx/.tsx or .c through the real multiplexer.
findings.consequence: Document identifier is typescript for JS/JSX/TSX and cpp for C, losing normal javascript/javascriptreact/typescriptreact/c distinctions; server parser/mode selection can be wrong.
findings.suggestedFix: Separate profile/toolchain routing ID from protocol document language ID, with explicit per-extension mapping and negotiation where supported.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Capture correct didOpen identifiers for JS/JSX/TS/TSX/C/C++; exercise real TypeScript server JS and JSX navigation in a fixture.
findings.observedEvidence: Evidence/07-probes.json records grouped identifiers in all four tested didOpen messages.
findings.inferenceLimits: Actual TypeScript-server misparse was not measured; some servers infer parser mode from URI and tolerate wrong IDs.
findings.markdownParagraph: MEDIUM — The multiplexer sends profile IDs directly in `didOpen` (`lsp-multiplexer.ts:1040,1437`). The probe sent `typescript` for JavaScript, JSX and TSX, and `cpp` for C. Toolchain grouping is useful for prompts but loses protocol document distinctions. Map source suffixes to canonical document IDs and test real JSX/JavaScript server behavior; the downstream impact remains server-dependent.

findings.title: Server-originated JSON-RPC requests receive no response

evidence.detail: Every message with method is ignored, including messages with request id.
Initialize waits for a correlated response under timeout.

findings.trigger: Peer sends a client request requiring a reply while an operation awaits server progress; even unsupported requests need a JSON-RPC error response.
findings.consequence: Peer awaiting client response can stall until startup/request timeout; notifications and requests are indistinguishable to this adapter.
findings.suggestedFix: Dispatch supported client requests and reply with typed method-not-found to unsupported requests. Keep workspace mutation requests outside this read-only adapter/pair06 boundary.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Fake peer waiting on a string-ID callback receives exactly one result/error; initialize/query settles; true notifications remain non-correlated and do not reject pending requests.
findings.observedEvidence: Evidence/07-probes.json: peer-issued configuration request received0 replies; initialize timed out after40ms.
findings.inferenceLimits: This is a conditional protocol-liveness failure; no claim is made that a specific installed supported server emitted this callback.
findings.markdownParagraph: MEDIUM — All incoming messages carrying `method` are ignored (`lsp-multiplexer.ts:539`), including requests with IDs. A peer waiting for a client response in the probe received none and timed out. Implement bounded client-request dispatch and explicit errors for unsupported methods while keeping notifications non-correlated. This confirms a protocol gap; it does not prove a particular installed server currently triggers it.

findings.title: Explicit Rust crate imports resolve caller-local modules before crate-root modules

evidence.detail: crate:: prefix is detected then removed.
Resolution first joins the remaining path to importing file directory.
Crate root is only a fallback after caller-local match.
This resolver creates file-reference graph edges.

findings.trigger: src/nested/main.rs imports crate::config and both src/config.rs and src/nested/config.rs exist.
findings.consequence: Import graph chooses nested/config.rs, contradicting explicit crate rooting and misleading reference/impact navigation.
findings.suggestedFix: Resolve crate:: exclusively relative to the owning Cargo crate root; preserve correct self/super/local mod rules and nested-workspace ownership.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Two config files fixture must select src/config.rs; add two-crate workspace and crate-specific module-root fixtures.
findings.inferenceLimits: Resolver is heuristic, not a Rust compiler; the wrong explicit-root result is still deterministic.
findings.markdownParagraph: MEDIUM — Rust strips `crate::` and tries the caller’s directory before crate root (`import-resolution.ts:275,281,289`). With both root and nested `config.rs`, the explicit crate import incorrectly selected the nested file. Resolve against the owning crate first, then test `self`, `super`, local modules and multiple crates. This is a deterministic heuristic graph error, independently of missing compiler integration.

findings.title: Go import resolution can create a reference to a foreign-language file

evidence.detail: Go import is gated by root go.mod identity.
Suffix search scans every indexed path without extension filtering.
One foreign suffix candidate is accepted as file target.
Accepted result becomes file-to-file references edge.

findings.trigger: Go imports local module/pkg/config while that directory contains only an indexed main.ts and no Go source.
findings.consequence: An unrelated TypeScript file satisfies the package-directory suffix and becomes a fabricated cross-language import edge.
findings.suggestedFix: Use Go-package metadata or at least exact normalized directory plus .go candidates; represent multi-file package ownership without arbitrary one-file guessing.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Foreign-only directory must stay unresolved; valid Go package maps to package/member evidence; external, ambiguous and nested-module cases remain honest.
findings.inferenceLimits: No real go list execution was needed to demonstrate wrong file selection.
findings.markdownParagraph: MEDIUM — Go’s suffix search scans every indexed file (`import-resolution.ts:359`) and accepts a lone matching directory member (`:370`). A fixture with only `pkg/config/main.ts` resolved a Go package import to that TypeScript file. Restrict candidates to the owning Go package and model package membership explicitly. Cross-language references require bridge evidence; sharing a directory suffix is insufficient.

domainAssessment.security: Observed containment before LSP document-byte reads, safe SCIP relative paths, fixed argv diagnostic commands, checksum-pinned/byte-bounded grammar repair and safe interpolated build tokens. No demonstrated injection or credential leak. Language-server process access itself is a host boundary, not an OS sandbox; those policy paths belong execution/governance shards.
domainAssessment.correctness: Confirmed wrong call/import/precise-reference edges, stale LSP document views, incorrect root selection, misleading diagnostic success and missing installed query assets. Each uses exact current source anchors plus bounded fixture evidence where possible.
domainAssessment.state-mutation: Shared parser cache keeps grammar through query failure; separate LSP version stores diverge; restart/disposal loses child ownership; silent skipped-sync paths stay dirty. No WorkspaceEdit mutation application findings duplicated from pair06.
domainAssessment.error-handling: Good typed unavailable/TCP/protocol statuses and scoped-validation drift/re-attestation failures coexist with ignored server requests, discarded diagnostic status and LSP malformed-frame teardown without termination. Binary grammar repair lacks caller cancellation and can honor long Retry-After delays.
domainAssessment.performance: Bounds and asynchronous shared caches are implemented, not assumed. Fake child counts confirm an ownership leak despite bounded pool counts. Opened document map has no explicit cap. Owning-target build graph still synchronously probes cargo/go up to10s per process on live tool path; no latency benchmark was run.
domainAssessment.dependency-hygiene: web-tree-sitter0.25.10, @vscode grammars0.1.4 and build grammar package0.1.13 are explicitly declared/pinned; GDScript immutable asset/ABI provenance is explicit. Packaging omits query assets; current bundler resolves a runtime package probe to build-checkout path. No registry/network vulnerability audit or dependency installation performed.
domainAssessment.test-coverage: Root evidence154pass/4fail and isolated17pass/3fail is environment-specific; current pinned explicit grammar probes repair the interpretation. Several mocks miss real component interactions: two collapsed language families, long SCIP prefix collision, query->first-sync version and restart->dispose ownership. Eleven argv cases and skip-gated clangd do not establish eleven-server assurance. Packaged query script only warns on missing expected tokens and is not fresh isolated-install evidence.
domainAssessment.api-contract: ManifestV1 is deterministic/detached with closed language keys and golden validation; do not treat listed tool names/stages as negotiated runtime availability. Preserve setWasmDir relative/verbatim API. LSP document language IDs and monotonic versions break protocol expectations; diagnostic passed scalar lacks coverage/outcome contract. Existing constructed-only service interface additions are explicitly documented and not separately flagged as newly discovered breakage.

Root tests154pass/4fail and isolated17pass/3fail are retained as existing evidence, not renamed release failures. Pinned local asset probes succeeded for PHP/Swift/Kotlin/GDScript. Fresh component bundles are not a packed whole SDK installation.

WorkspaceEdit mutation normalization/apply/version/resource operations remain pair06. Pair08 owns SCIP/index manager persistence/refresh/snapshot semantics. Execution sandbox/approval, native sidecar supervisors, broad retrieval ranking and global learned-routing audits are elsewhere.

Cross-language generated-schema/RPC/FFI absence is scoped to inspected target-language consumers. Whole-repo implementations outside this slice and live virtual-FS/server namespace consistency remain unknown.
